summary: Implemented the terminal window title setting, without running tests, installing packages, or committing. Changes: rich/segment.py adds ControlType.SET_WINDOW_TITLE = 16 and a Tuple[ControlType, str] member in the ControlCode union. rich/control.py adds the format entry "\x1b]0;{title}\x07" and the Control.title(title) classmethod, which passes one two-item code. rich/console.py adds set_window_title(title) beside show_cursor; it buffers the control only when is_terminal is true and returns that bool, with a Google-style docstring. rich/_windows_renderer.py adds one elif branch calling term.set_title(title). CHANGELOG.md gains an Unreleased Added bullet linking pull request 2200. Tests added: a forced-terminal console test skipped on Windows, a Control.title test, and a Windows-only renderer test asserting set_title is called once with "Hello, world!". Not verified by execution: Black formatting, mypy, and the test suite; all checks were by reading. Choices made: set-title maps to the existing LegacyWindowsTerm.set_title method, and other render paths needed no change because _render_buffer already drops control segments when not a terminal.
